findings.title: No test for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware
findings.body: The logic that adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname to the context moved here from MetricsMiddleware. The old coverage was in the metrics middleware tests. I found no test in this PR that checks the new middleware puts these attributes on the context. A small test would catch a regression in the moved logic or in the middleware order in pluginsintegration.go.

contracts.action: LoggerMiddleware now logs through m.logger.FromContext(ctx) instead of appending pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID and traceID by hand
contracts.equivalent_path: Before this change, logRequest built those fields itself. Now the same fields come from the contextual attributes set by ContextualLoggerMiddleware, plus the tracing provider registered in pkg/infra/tracing/tracing.go:91.
contracts.before_after: ContextualLoggerMiddleware is registered before LoggerMiddleware at pluginsintegration.go:159-161, so the context carries the attributes when logRequest runs. I did not read the body of the tracing provider to confirm it emits the traceID key.
contracts.visible_effect: The 'Plugin Request Completed' log line should keep the same fields. The only difference is that traceID now comes from the provider.
contracts.failure_mode: If the tracing provider does not emit the key traceID, or uses a different key name, traceID disappears from these logs without any error. FromContext in pkg/plugins/log/logger.go:48-56 falls back to a plain logger when the type assertion fails, and that case is silent too.
contracts.open_question: Does the provider at pkg/infra/tracing/tracing.go:91 emit a 'traceID' key with the same name as before?

summary: The refactor moves contextual-logger setup into its own middleware and renames the instrumentation middleware to MetricsMiddleware. Middleware order is correct. One open question: whether the traceID field is still logged, which depends on the tracing provider I did not read. I also suggest a test for the new middleware. I found no other implementers of the plugin Logger interface that the new method would break.
